# Agentic IAM with Vault

@include 'alerts/beta.mdx'

@include 'alerts/enterprise-and-hcp.mdx'

Vault Enterprise enables AI agents to obtain fine-grained access to secrets stored in Vault that based on the intersection of Vault policies and Rich Authorization Request (RAR) claims specified in access token granted by an authorization server.

The authorization server may be a component of an IDP or a distinct authorization server. This process ensures least-privileged, ephemeral permissions to the agent in scenarios where the agent is acting on its own or on behalf of a user.

Using a least-privilege approach implements zero trust principles by ensuring
agent credentials are ephemeral and narrowly scoped through delegation.

The agent acts on behalf of a human developer and receives an effective
permission set that is the intersection of three independent controls:

1. Human baseline ACL policies define what the person can do

1. Agent ceiling policies from the Vault Agent Registry cap the maximum
   the agent can ever do

1. Per-session RAR claims carried in the token specify what one session
   may access

For example, you can configure IBM Verify to function as an authorization server.
IBM Verify then issues OAuth RAR tokens to an agent or other AI applcation, which
that agent or application can then use to authenticate with Vault.


## How the request flow works

Vault acts as an OAuth Resource Server and validates the OAuth-JWT token
received by the agent from the Verify IDP authorization server.  The AI agent
is registered with Vault in the Vault Registry, so the Vault is aware of the
agent's identity as entity and associated policies.

<Tip>

Review the
[Rich authorization requests (RAR)](/vault/docs/ai/oauth-server/rar/) overview
for a deeper dive into how RAR works with Vault.

</Tip>
